record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What conditions on asymptotically flat initial data guarantee that the null infinity of the resulting Einstein initial-value-problem solution is regular enough for the Penrose extended manifold to exist with at least a C3 metric, so that the peeling theorem holds?

evidence.quote: Determine conditions on AF initial data which ensure that the null infinity of the resulting solution of the IVP is sufficiently regular that the Penrose extended manifold exists, with at least C3 metric so the peeling theorem holds [PRl].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein initial-value problem for an asymptotically flat (AF) initial data set $(\Sigma, h, K)$, where $\Sigma$ is a 3-manifold, $h$ a Riemannian metric, and $K$ a symmetric 2-tensor satisfying the vacuum constraint equations, with $(h, K)$ tending to flat data at a suitable rate at spatial infinity. Let $(M, g)$ denote the maximal vacuum Cauchy development. The Penrose conformal compactification associates to $(M, g)$ an extended manifold $(\tilde M, \tilde g)$ with $\tilde g = \Omega^2 g$ and a boundary $\mathscr{I}$ (null infinity) at which $\Omega = 0$ and $d\Omega \ne 0$.

Problem: Determine explicit conditions on the asymptotically flat initial data $(h, K)$ that guarantee that the resulting development admits a Penrose extended manifold $(\tilde M, \tilde g)$ on which the conformal metric $\tilde g$ is of regularity at least $C^3$ in a neighborhood of null infinity $\mathscr{I}$, and consequently that the peeling theorem holds, i.e., along outgoing null geodesics the Weyl tensor components decay as
$$\Psi_k = O(r^{k-5}), \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4,$$
where $r$ is an affine parameter along the null geodesic and $\Psi_k$ are the Newman–Penrose Weyl scalars.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of identifying conditions on AF initial data ensuring peeling at null infinity has seen substantial partial progress. Friedrich's work near spatial infinity (gr-qc/0701049) and subsequent results using conformal methods give sufficient (often very restrictive) conditions; recent work (e.g., Hintz–Vasy, and 2025 results "From spatial to null infinity: Connecting initial data to peeling") characterizes peeling in terms of Sobolev-type regularity of the data near spatial infinity. A complete, sharp characterization of AF data guaranteeing a $C^3$ Penrose-extended metric and full classical peeling remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Regularity at space-like and null infinity
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions on the free initial data near space-like infinity are derived which ensure that for solutions developing from these data singularities in the conformal structure cannot occur.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient (partial) conditions are known on initial data to avoid conformal-structure singularities at null infinity.

status_evidence.title: From spatial to null infinity: Connecting initial data to peeling
status_evidence.snippet: A unified expansion of the metric in a neighborhood of spatial infinity that includes a piece of null infinity can connect the asymptotic expansions of solutions to Einstein's equations in the different asymptotic regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work connects asymptotic conditions on initial data to peeling, indicating ongoing partial progress.

status_evidence.title: The conformal approach to asymptotic analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Penrose compactification and energy estimates provides a definition of the peeling at all orders in terms of Sobolev regularity near null infinity ... characterize completely the classes of initial data ensuring a certain order of peeling.
status_evidence.claim: Sobolev-type characterizations of peeling classes are available, but a sharp characterization for the C^3 Penrose extension remains incomplete.
